claims_checked.result: Bounded C1 for d>=3; bounded planar Lipschitz; separate C1,alpha gradient bound. Exterior only |lambda|>lambda0 with bounded weak velocity and pressure bounded at infinity. Additive pressure gauge retained.

g=div(u phi) has mean zero and belongs to the negative Sobolev class. One common beta is permitted. Boundary scaling (Nr)^((d-1)/q)*(Nr)^(-1/q')=(Nr)^(d/q-1). Fixed-ball arbitrary-slope defect has explicit graph-box repair.
r=R|lambda|^-1/2, q>d, N large, and |lambda|>16 r0^-2 N4 give permissible chart radii. Complementary frequency estimate3.25 consistent. No circular parameter choice.

M_q only averages scales >=r. Annular decay 2^-jsigma and j2^-jsigma summable. q'<=2 Neumann and q>=2 scalar Dirichlet ranges compatible. Fixed upper-cutoff convention handled by fixed-scale/global boundary norms.

Tangential derivative flux vanishes; mean-zero auxiliary data valid. Exterior p normalization and Lemma5.3 mean estimate retained; planar zero flux removes logarithmic mode. Outer-sphere terms vanish with stated harmonic decay.

grad p normal identity has no missing 1/2. On approximants h_l=-lambda u dot n_l retained, converges uniformly0 when u continuouszero trace. Collar divergence gives exact zero flux, no global velocity integrability assumption. Finite-q traces pass via A.4–A.8.
Local compactness and normalized harmonic pressure used with annular control/zero flux. No inference that a bare 1/r gradient bound alone implies bounded pressure.

Printed W0^{1,infinity} class stronger than theorem. Homogeneous bounded stationary forcing gives local W1,q with q>d (planar q slightly>2), finite-q boundary gradients and traces. Compact-boundary cover, continuity, p->beta, collar flux and absorption give the intended bounded-weak uniqueness. Report supplies this completion; no separate nonuniqueness finding.

Sneiberg interval near2 overlaps boundary regularity at some q>2; exponent2/q-1 negative. Main velocity proof does not use all-q gradient assertion. C0 on C0_sigma distinguished from non-C0 Linfinity semigroup; exterior uniform boundedness explicitly not established.
